mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for three consecutive months indicates a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous 4-month average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction relative to the prior four-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicate accelerating labor market weakness, which amplifies recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >3% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the producer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for three consecutive months signals broad-based inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 4% for three consecutive months.
